speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; please tell me, how many days old are you and when did these symptoms start?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The history of bilious vomiting starting immediately in a term infant is highly concerning for a distal intestinal obstruction, such as malrotation with midgut volvulus. Given your brother's history of pyloric stenosis, could you confirm if your baby has passed meconium within the first 24 hours of life?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray (Upright to look for pneumobilia)
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal X-Ray: 'Double bubble' sign indicative of duodenal atresia; Abdominal Ultrasound: Not performed

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia. The "double bubble" sign on the X-ray confirms a proximal duodenal obstruction, which is consistent with the clinical presentation of bilious vomiting in a newborn. Given your family history of pyloric stenosis, we must also rule out concurrent midgut volvulus, but the primary diagnosis is duodenal atresia.
